bullets.title: S&P 500 logs worst week since April 2025, 7-day losing streak
bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 8.61% for the week (worst since April 2025), closing Friday as the seventh consecutive daily decline—the longest streak since February 2020. The Nasdaq fell 10.02% and is now down YTD after hitting an ATH October 6. Breadth was extremely weak with decliners outnumbering gainers by >15:1 on the week. All major indices broke below their 200-day moving averages.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness is the key macro shock—Waller signals possible 50bp December hike
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller suggested a 50bp hike in December and advocated for hikes in December and January to break inflationary psychology, while Goolsbee called inflation 'borderline disturbing.' The market was previously pricing comfort with ~2.5% PCE tolerance; Fed rhetoric now signals 2.0% target is non-negotiable. Market pricing shifted to 62bps of additional hikes over 10 months, and the traditional 'Fed put' tied to equity/credit stress may no longer apply if inflation credibility is the priority.

bullets.title: AI trade broad unwind: semis down 17%, hedge fund tech selling at decade-worst pace
bullets.body: The SOX index fell 17.1% this week (6th decline in 7 weeks), and the AI Infrastructure index fell 15% w/w and is -46% from ATH. Hedge funds were net sellers of global equities at a -4.4 z-score pace over six weeks—the fastest in a decade—with semis the most net-sold group for 2 months running. HF net leverage dropped to the 26th percentile over 5 years; L/S at 21st percentile globally, with nets in the low 40s and gross at 195%. Rotation into defensives (Utilities, Telecom, Pharma, Staples) is at levels not seen since the dot-com bust.

bullets.title: NVDA beats but stock drops ~47% from ATH; SEC probe and leadership vacuum weigh
bullets.body: Nvidia reported Q3 revenue of $115.84B (+103% y/y), beat consensus by ~6%, and raised FY28 revenue growth guidance to ~75% from ~70%. However, the stock is down ~47% from its all-time high due to: (1) the SEC opening a civil probe into potential accounting/disclosure issues; (2) CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and board ruling out his reinstatement while searching for a successor; (3) the company halting H200 chip shipments to China (~$2.4B in quarterly revenue) under new BIS export controls; (4) NVDA signaling more selective neocloud financing. Supply commitments rose to $390B but >$100B for FY28, with limited FY29 visibility.

bullets.title: New US BIS chip export controls tighten: SE Asia licenses, remote-access ban, TSMC/Samsung halt
bullets.body: The Commerce Department issued an interim final rule requiring export licenses for advanced semiconductor sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, and banned overseas data centers from remotely renting AI compute to China-linked entities without a license. TSMC and Samsung suspended advanced chip (≤16nm) shipments to Chinese customers pending compliance. The Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule was rescinded. Analysts estimate the rules remove 1-2 GW (~10%) of near-term AI chip demand, with NVDA bearing the most direct exposure.

bullets.title: Data center policy headwinds compound: state moratoriums, Trump overseas DC tax penalty, permitting
bullets.body: The Trump administration announced it would tax US companies building data centers abroad, triggering a sell-off in data center names (DLR -9.73% for the week). Loudon County, VA adopted a 12-month data center pause. Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa pledged a new data center permit moratorium (while TCEQ resumed permits for in-progress projects). Arizona, North Carolina, and Georgia also introduced new regulatory hurdles. Meanwhile, the Senate passed energy permitting reform to ease large-scale infrastructure approvals, partially offsetting headwinds.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers face $595B funding gap through 2028; JPM downgrades GOOGL to Neutral
bullets.body: JPM models aggregate hyperscaler FCF turning negative through 2028 with a ~$595B funding gap, requiring $450B in AI-related debt/equity supply in 2027 alone. JPM downgraded Alphabet to Neutral from Overweight citing Search durability concerns and tighter valuations, while retaining Overweight on AMZN and ORCL. NVDA's pullback from 'bank of AI' ecosystem financing raises capital cost risks for neoclouds. SemiAnalysis separately cut 2028-30 AI accelerator spend by 28-41%, removing ~$1.6T from cumulative 2027-2030 projections—primarily driven by pricing deflation, not demand collapse.

bullets.title: Equities now at tactical oversold with key indicators: SPX at 7-decade-low relative PE, options skew at highs
bullets.body: MS QDS notes the S&P had only 8 prior 7-consecutive-day losing streaks since 1985 with average positive returns forward but 50% saw further declines. SPX Put/Call vol spread hit a 10-year extreme (9.66, highest <10% of time), historically associated with +3.6% 2-month returns (1.73x Sharpe). Systematic net leverage fell to the 25th percentile (from 80th in early October). Pensions forecast to buy ~$50B at current prices; $40B macro systematic supply expected over the next week. NVDA now trades at ~10x forward P/E vs. 5-year average of 33x.

bullets.title: Cross-asset signals: gold -9.5%, copper -9.9%, Bitcoin -15.5%—real yield shock propagating
bullets.body: Gold logged its worst week since March, copper fell 9.9% (6th straight week lower), Bitcoin fell 15.5% (7th straight week lower) near 2-year lows, and WTI crude was down 5.8%. The dollar index reached 52-week highs. Real 2-year yields have risen 73bp over 13 weeks, a regime historically associated with risk-asset stress. These cross-asset moves signal the real-rate shock is still propagating; analysts note reversal in dollar/crypto/commodities would signal the hiking cycle is nearing an end.

bullets.title: US housing at multi-decade lows: NAHB at 14-year low, pending home sales at record low
bullets.body: November NAHB homebuilder sentiment fell to 14-year lows. October pending home sales missed, hitting new historical lows (-4.7% m/m), with existing home sales tracking toward 3.6M annualized—the lowest since 2010. Building permits declined 8.9% m/m to their lowest since 2022. Mortgage rates rose to 7.35% (30-year). Analysts expect flat to modest further decline in housing activity in 2027.

bullets.title: October retail sales beat; consumer resilience narrative holds despite macro headwinds
bullets.body: October control-group retail sales came in at +0.6% m/m (vs. +0.3% consensus), with August and September each revised up ~37bp. Real PCE is tracking ~2.5% annualized in Q4 vs. Bloomberg consensus of 2.0%. BofA data shows holiday spending is off to a strong start. Consumer earnings (WMT, TGT, TJX) supported the resilience thesis, though BBWI cut Q4 guidance on inflation and competitive pressures.

bullets.title: Hedge fund capitulation not yet confirmed; retail was a net buyer of ~$29B in equities
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs estimates $57B in CTA selling over the last month, with systematic net leverage declining from the 80th to 25th percentile. Retail net bought ~$29B in US equities despite the drawdown, while corporates buyback breadth was at YTD highs with 70 companies active. The pattern of large HF net selling coinciding with a market sell-off has historically been followed by a rebound within a month, but that pattern has not yet confirmed in this cycle.

bullets.title: Anthropic (ANT) IPO priced at $83; raised record $81.3B but failed to revive AI trade
bullets.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83/share (above the $70-78 range), with a fully diluted valuation of ~$1.5T and a first-day opening at $111.50 that faded back near IPO price by Friday. The IPO was nearly 7x oversubscribed. Despite validating AI demand, the IPO did not revive the AI trade—NVDA continued to fall and the broader tech selloff persisted. Some analysts note large IPOs typically decline 30-50% in the first year.

bullets.title: US-China tech tensions intensify: MATCH Act, TSMC/Samsung halt, retaliation risk rising
bullets.body: The Commerce Department closed the TSMC/Samsung self-certification loophole for China chip exports and issued rules restricting Chinese chip designers from working with foreign foundries. The MATCH Act (restricting ASML tool exports to China) is odds-on for NDAA inclusion. China is reportedly considering rare-earth retaliation. The Trump-Xi-Putin APEC meeting in Shenzhen produced no mention of Ukraine and committed to increased refined petroleum production but no tech truce. Mid-December Trump-Xi G20 meeting is a key diplomatic catalyst.

bullets.title: Geopolitical escalation: Ukraine destroys Kerch Bridge; Russian retaliation underway
bullets.body: Ukraine destroyed the Kerch Bridge (a major military and logistics asset), triggering Russian missile and drone retaliation including strikes in neighboring Poland—which the Trump administration dismissed as 'a couple of little missiles, by mistake.' The EU is discussing an additional €45B in Ukraine aid. Cyber security events are increasing in frequency and are viewed as a broadly adverse supply shock likely inflationary in direction; central bank response remains data-dependent.

bullets.title: AI users outperform non-users on margins and productivity—favorable factor positioning
bullets.body: Real sales per employee for S&P 1500 hit a record high and accelerated over the past two quarters. Companies with clear AI usage and top-quintile margin sentiment have significantly outperformed; forward net margin expectations for AI users continue to rise even as non-AI user expectations decline. 22V and Goldman recommend staying long high-AI-usage companies, particularly in services ex-software, as the best positioning amid the broader macro slowdown.

bullets.title: MS raises S&P 500 year-end 2027 target to 8,700 on earnings and AI capex durability
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley CIO Mike Wilson raised the 12-month S&P 500 price target to 8,700 (19x forward EPS of $458) based on healthy EPS growth (2026 +34%, 2027 +14%), lower oil, stabilizing rate volatility, and broadening AI adoption (44% of S&P 500 companies cited quantifiable AI benefits). Goldman Sachs also targets 8,700 for year-end 2027. Street consensus price targets cluster around 8,700, implying 20%+ upside from current levels. JPM maintains its SPX year-end 2026 target at 8,000.

bullets.title: JPM 2027 US macro: Fed hikes to 4.5-4.75%, AI capex moderates, consumer slows
bullets.body: JPMorgan's 2027 US economic outlook forecasts three additional Fed hikes (December, January, March) taking the funds rate to 4.5-4.75%, followed by cuts in 2028. AI-related spending growth moderates from 10% (2026) to 8% (2027), and real consumer spending slows from 2.6% to 1.7% as wealth effects diminish. Core PCE stays in the mid-to-high 2% range. AI is estimated to contribute ~0.5pp/year to productivity, with labor productivity growth accelerating to 2.5% annualized since start of 2024.

bullets.title: Taiwan and Korea semi exports peaking; global AI capex cycle mid-stage with slowing momentum
bullets.body: Taiwan October export orders hit record highs (+78% y/y) but actual shipments growth is peaking. Korea's semiconductor business confidence is declining alongside falling equity markets (Nikkei -22% from AI bubble peak, Taiwan -18% for the week). Semiconductor sales growth is expected to slow from 2026's +108% y/y to just +29% in 2027. PSC Macro's Nancy Lazar flags AI cycle mid-stage indicators: peaking revenue growth, weakening FCF, rising competition, and slowing capex. Jefferies cuts NVDA PT to $250 citing 2028 demand uncertainty.
